To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

patients initiated on angiotension-converting enzyme inhibitors or β-blockers had a slightly higher rate of blood pressure control than patients initiated on a thiazide diuretic, that the use of fixed-dose combination (FDC) antihypertensives was more effective in the initial control of hypertension than either free-equivalent combination (FEC) therapy or monotherapy, and that the use of FDC therapy was more effective than monotherapy in the initial control hypertension in patients with diabetes

the use of fixed-dose combination antihypertensives as initial therapy was more effective than monotherapy or free-equivalent combinations in the control of blood pressure in a primary care population.

patients initiated on an angio-tensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor or a β-blockers had higher rates of blood-pressure control, and that fixed-dose combinations were more effective in the treatment of hypertension than either monotherapy or free-equivalent combinations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the comparative effectiveness of different antihypertensives in a large primary care population.
comparative effectiveness studies of therapeutic classes and treatment strategies in hypertension.
the development and evaluation of new methods for the analysis of large data sets and their application to the study of the effectiveness of antihypertensives in a primary care setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of FDC is the best initial treatment for hypertension.
FDCs are more efficacious than FECs and monotherapy.
the use of FDC therapy is the most effective approach in the initiation of therapy for the treatment of hypertension.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors and beta blockers as initial therapy is slightly better for blood pressure control than thiazide diuretics and that fixed dose combinations are more effective in the initial treatment of patients than monotherapy.
the use of FDC is more effective than monotherapy in the control of blood pressure.
FDCs are more effective than FECs and monotherapy in the treatment of hypertension in primary care.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FDCs should be used as the initial antihypertensives in patients with stage 1 hypertension.
FDCs are more effective than FECs in the control of blood pressure and in attaining blood pressure goals.
the initial use of an FDC is more effective than the initial use of a FEC or monotherapy in the control of blood pressure.
